Mobile recovery runs in the C++ CLI, with no Python interpreter or deployed helper directory. Android defaults to NeverD builtin DEX/smali readers, register verification and Java emission; it needs no external decompiler or JVM at runtime. Only explicit --jadx selects the separately installed compatibility backend. ZIP decompression uses zlib.

Builtin Android emits verified Java dispatch bodies for its supported DEX/smali subset, with complete per-input method accounting and separate native/abstract declarations. Unsupported bodies reject the transaction; no backend fallback or placeholder body is used. Resources and native libraries are excluded.

Builtin Android is experimental, not a guarantee for arbitrary APKs or all bytecode. Generic/dynamic invocation, monitor operations, unproven initialization, unsupported annotations, unavailable local member bindings, and non-representable Java declarations are rejected. Original source text and compilation-lost information cannot be recovered. Generation uses conservative byte, work and time budgets.

Android acceptance recompiles generated source without original classes and compares behavior against independently compiled owned fixtures. JDK and D8 are test tools only. iOS retains LLVM/Capstone dependencies and uses LLVMSwiftDemangle from the NeverD LLVM fork for in-process structured Swift signature demangling. Fork source builds and matching LLVM packages include this component; NeverD does not fetch a separate Swift source dependency or require an installed Swift compiler/toolchain to build or run. Independent Swift behavior tests require swiftc.
iOS emits native C and reconstructs supported Objective-C and Swift bodies from actual HighIR on arm64 and x86_64, with independently reported callable and metadata coverage.

Proven Swift compiler-generated entries project into recovered type source and remain in the callable inventory. Native method bodies and compiler projections have separate counts and explicit source-representation evidence.

Source recovery requires supported scalar/stack ABI bindings, storage layouts, and complete native dependency groups. Unsupported aggregate, variadic, generic, asynchronous, throwing, or unresolved runtime paths remain explicitly unrecovered.
Runtime type hints guide source projection; they do not authenticate an ABI or prove semantic equivalence. Original comments and compilation-lost information cannot be recovered.

Encrypted native slices are rejected. Unresolved metadata and pointer encodings reduce coverage. Swift source signatures use the built-in LLVM component and are checked against native symbol entries; metadata-only runs neither the native source exporter nor signature demangling. Signature inventory records demangler {name: llvm-swift-demangle, execution: builtin, version: 6.3.3}. No external demangler or toolchain-discovery process or logs are used; the former executable option and environment setting are removed.

Overall success records output publication, not complete method recovery. Recovered coverage requires every inventoried callable to have its supported body or proven compiler projection; incomplete metadata can still make overall coverage partial or unknown. An exhaustive original-program inventory is not guaranteed.

Metadata-only emits declarations, metadata and the selected binary, without native C, Objective-C bodies or method-body coverage. Full recovery analyzes one selected native artifact, and max-func can leave discovered methods unrecovered.

requires NEVERD_ENABLE_DRIVER_EMULATION=ON; this opt-in profile executes x64 WDM initialization and explicitly requested create, buffered/direct IOCTL, read/write, cleanup, close, configured AddDevice/resource-free or register-bank PnP, explicit pageable Query/Set power and unload phases through Unicorn, without host kernel loading or host OS API forwarding

only the documented native PE32+ loading profile and finite kernel API subset are modeled; unknown imports are lazy traps and stop at first execution or exported-data read, while unmodeled CPU environment operations, opaque object state, malformed images and unsupported loader requirements fail explicitly

WDM stacks contain guest-owned DEVICE_OBJECTs and optionally a separately owned scenario PDO. IoAttachDeviceToDeviceStack returns the previous top and derives StackSize/AlignmentRequirement without changing the NextDevice inventory or buffer flags. IoDetachDevice receives the saved lower at PASSIVE_LEVEL; attach permits DISPATCH_LEVEL. Named lower FILE_OBJECT/report identity stays distinct from top dispatch and top READ/WRITE flags; retained routes survive detach/delete through dispatch return. Internal holds do not inflate the open-handle ReferenceCount.

IofCallDriver and the IoCallDriver helper dispatch to the exact retained target; genuine inline Copy/Skip/SetCompletion operate on the original bounded guest IRP stack. Completion clears consumed lower slots before upper callbacks and separates lower NTSTATUS, callback control results and final IoStatus. Success/error/cancel masks and pending propagation are modeled, including propagation after STATUS_PENDING dispatch returns; invoked callbacks own propagation. STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED and nested completion preserve packet/MDL/buffer lifetime until terminal unwind, with exactly-once retirement.

KernelGuestCall uses subsystem-owner tags and local tokens for nested WDM/WDF continuations, preserving parent CPU frames and inherited IRQL. WDF attachment/forwarding, attachment to live stacks, intermediate detach, changed forwarded major functions, targets outside retained routes, driver-allocated IRPs, additional PnP operations and other hardware/resource models remain unsupported.

Optional genuine-WDK driver_wdm_stack.c images use NEVERD_WDM_STACK_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_STACK_CFG_FIXTURE. Model/native/public tests cover Copy and Skip, buffered READ/WRITE and file lifecycle, IOCTL completion ordering, worker/DPC completion, MPR waits with direct MDLs, nested completion, malformed cursors and normal/active-CFG rebasing. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; evidence remains Linux-only.

Public DriverPnp.h and DeviceLifecycle.def own lifecycle enums; pnp_devices explicitly supplies up to 64 unique case-sensitive ASCII IDs of 1-64 bytes (leading alphanumeric, then alphanumeric/_/-/.), resource_free or register_bank bus, D0 device power and working system power. No missing hardware/power facts are guessed. Ordinary device_id and device selectors are exclusive; PnP requires device_id, minor and bus_completion and rejects file/transfer/cancellation fields even when zero. JSON/native preflight share the same contract.

The eight public common PnP minors are Start, QueryRemove, CancelRemove, Remove, QueryStop, Stop, CancelStop and SurpriseRemoval. Every configured bus completion requires an explicit final 32-bit status, rejects STATUS_PENDING, and accepts optional nonnegative delay_100ns through INT64_MAX from actual provider receipt. Stop/CancelStop/SurpriseRemoval/CancelRemove/Remove require exactly STATUS_SUCCESS (0). Shared devicePnpFinalStatusError validates both configured bus policy and final guest completion. QueryStop STATUS_RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED (0x119) is explicitly unsupported because it requests resource requery. Other PnP operations, general power policy, resource rebalance, relations/capabilities, general hardware and broader KMDF PnP remain unsupported.

After successful DriverEntry, each configured PDO invokes the actual guest AddDevice callback once in add_device:<ID>. Provider-owned PDO/DRIVER_OBJECT inventory remains separate from the guest driver and cannot be deleted, mutated or impersonated by guest code. Successful filters may decline attachment. Failed AddDevice records its status and retires only a clean provider; new guest devices left behind, including detached leaks, cause ModelError without fabricated cleanup.

PnP IRPs share the existing captured route, guest stack and completion authority; they are KernelMode, file-free and initially STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED. Only actual provider receipt consumes the configured response; timed completion participates in the virtual scheduler without inventing a guest callback. Final upper completion owns lifecycle commit/rollback and may differ from the recorded bus status; successful PnP requires actual completed bus forwarding. Early Start/QueryStop/QueryRemove guest failure can leave bus observations null.

Ordinary CREATE/READ/WRITE/IOCTL/CLEANUP/CLOSE reach real guest dispatch outside Removing/Removed; model stop, remove-pending and power state do not synthesize an I/O refusal. Guest code may complete software operations, reject them or hold them. Immutable FDO/PDO and FILE_OBJECT lifecycle identity survives detach. Pending WDM transfers can overlap only through explicit batching across files or on one asynchronous file; a held IRP without a currently available producer still cannot wait for a later scenario start or cleanup request and is an explicit stalled ModelError. Normal Remove from Started still requires successful query; closed files and drained earlier requests before Remove are bounded-profile restrictions. Providers must be absent before unload; guest and provider retirement remain independent.

Reports preserve configuration.pnp_devices and observed pnp_devices id/pdo/add_device_status/attached/pnp_state/provider_present. Attached is current and false after removal. AddDevice failures affect scenario_success without replacing DriverEntry nt_status. Requests add nullable device_id/pnp; PnP file is null, with minor/state_before/state_after and nullable bus_status/bus_received_at_100ns/bus_completed_at_100ns. Configured status appears only at actual bus completion; receipt time is independent and legacy field types are preserved.

Original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_pnp.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_PNP_FIXTURE/NEVERD_WDM_PNP_CFG_FIXTURE; native normal/active-CFG rebasing covers AddDevice, file I/O, orderly/delayed removal, start/query failure and clean/leaking AddDevice failure. C API/CLI test seven-request delayed PnP reports. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; evidence remains Linux-only and does not establish general PnP/power support. Additional native cases exercise query-stop/cancel-stop/stop/restart, surprise removal, software I/O in pause/remove-pending states, guest failure after surprise, independent PDO/file identities, mixed AddDevice outcomes and an independent control device. C API/CLI normal/CFG execution also covers a 16-request stop/restart/surprise sequence and preflight rejection of resource requery.

KMDF caller-context preprocessing for buffered/direct/neither READ, WRITE and IOCTL runs at PASSIVE_LEVEL in the requestor process; the callback must complete or explicitly enqueue once before the configured default queue delivers I/O. For METHOD_NEITHER and neither READ/WRITE, unsafe accessors expose original scenario user buffers only there; WDF probe-and-lock checks page rights, pins request-owned physical bytes, and WdfMemoryGetBuffer returns a system alias usable by the queue outside requestor context. Completion releases aliases and pins; embedded user pointers and arbitrary user mappings remain unsupported.

KMDF 1.33 exact-version binding preserves real FxDriverEntry execution, separate WDFLDR module identity and 458 distinct function-table entries; only 69 documented table APIs plus WdfVersionBind/WdfVersionUnbind are modeled, and other reached entries remain unsupported_api traps; downlevel negotiation, class extensions and WdfLdrQueryInterface are unsupported

KMDF non-PnP drivers, generic objects, control devices, manual, sequential and finite or unlimited parallel default and nondefault queues, and incoming requests share typed contexts and guest cleanup/destroy callbacks at PASSIVE_LEVEL; nested continuations preserve caller CPU state and stack. Failed DriverEntry unregister cleans objects without EvtDriverUnload; adding references after cleanup is unsupported. Direct KMDF FDO/PDO pairs support resource-free and configured register-bank devices; WDF interrupt objects and automatic synchronization remain unmodeled; PnP queue stop/resume with driver-held requests remains unsupported.

KMDF PnP drivers execute EvtDriverDeviceAdd once per configured PDO with a framework-owned initializer. WdfDeviceCreate builds the direct FDO/PDO pair; WdfFdoInitWdmGetPhysicalDevice, WdfDeviceWdmGetPhysicalDevice, WdfDeviceWdmGetAttachedDevice, WdfWdmDeviceGetWdfDeviceHandle and WdfDeviceGetDriver preserve provider, stack and binding identity. A failed AddDevice automatically deletes created WDF devices and runs cleanup/destroy callbacks before provider retirement. Completed Remove runs WDF deletion before captured-route and PDO retirement. PnP queues accept WdfUseDefault/WdfTrue power management or WdfFalse driver-managed dispatch. WdfDeviceInitSetPnpPowerEventCallbacks accepts PrepareHardware, D0Entry, D0Exit and ReleaseHardware in the exact 144-byte KMDF 1.33 structure. Resource-free WDFCMRESLIST handles support GetCount=0 and GetDescriptor=NULL; configured register-bank lists expose read-only raw/translated CM_PARTIAL_RESOURCE_DESCRIPTOR entries through ReleaseHardware, then retire their guest storage. After provider START, PrepareHardware precedes D0Entry before IRP completion; failed PrepareHardware or D0Entry becomes the START status and still runs ReleaseHardware. STOP, surprise removal or removal from D0 runs D0Exit then ReleaseHardware before completion. Power-managed queues report WdfIoQueuePnpHeld outside D0 and resume after D0 entry. Unmodeled resource types, resource mutation, WDF interrupt objects, driver-held request stop/resume and other PnP events remain unsupported. A genuine WDK driver maps translated memory with MmMapIoSpace in PrepareHardware, unmaps it in ReleaseHardware, and final PnP completion rejects leaked mappings. The original WDK-linked driver_kmdf_pnp.c fixture covers normal/active-CFG rebasing, successful and failed AddDevice, start/file I/O/remove/unload and optional EvtDriverUnload via native and C API/CLI tests; evidence remains Linux-only.

Control devices require a copied printable-ASCII name and exact universal-access SDDL D:P(A;;GA;;;WD); other DACLs need an unmodeled caller token. Initializers are consumed only on success, partial creation is rolled back, and device/link ownership uses the WDM namespace; FinishInitializing gates delivery. Pending I/O or other live references prevent unsupported deletion/draining.

The 96-byte WDF_IO_QUEUE_CONFIG supports manual, sequential and finite or unlimited parallel default and nondefault queues with explicit passive/no-synchronization attributes; control-device queues are not power-managed, while PnP queues honor their tri-state power policy. Parallel dispatch uses NumberOfPresentedRequests=-1 for unlimited delivery or a positive finite limit. Requests beyond a finite or sequential presentation limit wait in FIFO order until a presented request completes, leaves the queue or is canceled. A manual default queue retains incoming requests without callback delivery. WdfIoQueueStop pauses delivery while still accepting requests; WdfIoQueueStart resumes waiting automatic callbacks, and WdfIoQueueGetState reports queued/delivered counts and readiness bits. Retrieval while stopped returns STATUS_WDF_PAUSED; a stop-completion callback receives its context after all previously delivered requests complete or leave the queue, while queued waiters do not block it; duplicate pending callback registration fails explicitly. WdfIoQueueDrain rejects new arrivals with STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_STATE while delivering already queued requests; its callback waits for both queued and driver-owned counts to reach zero, forwarding into a drained queue returns STATUS_WDF_BUSY, and WdfIoQueueStart restores acceptance. WdfIoQueuePurge also rejects arrivals, completes queued requests with STATUS_CANCELLED after cleanup, requests cancellation of marked driver-owned IRPs through their callbacks, and notifies only after queued, driver-owned and active cancel callback work has finished. WdfIoQueueStopSynchronously, WdfIoQueueDrainSynchronously and WdfIoQueuePurgeSynchronously suspend the caller until their respective delivered or queued-and-delivered work retires; purge waits through marked-request cancellation callbacks. A synchronous wait with no completion producer fails explicitly as stalled. WdfIoQueueStopAndPurge and WdfIoQueueStopAndPurgeSynchronously cancel requests queued at call time and marked driver-owned requests while keeping acceptance enabled and delivery paused. Later arrivals remain queued and do not delay the state callback or synchronous wait. Stop and StopSynchronously restore acceptance after a prior drain or purge. WdfRequestForwardToIoQueue transfers driver ownership to another same-device queue; an automatic destination presents its own matching callback when capacity permits, or completes with STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST after a slot opens if no handler matches. WdfIoQueueRetrieveNextRequest restores ownership from manual or sequential queues in FIFO order and returns STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES with NULL when empty; parallel retrieval returns STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_STATE. WdfRequestRequeue puts an unmarked retrieved request at the head of its manual queue. Cancellation of a still-queued request removes it and completes with STATUS_CANCELLED, executing cleanup callbacks before IRP retirement. Accepted requests mark the same IRP pending and return STATUS_PENDING independently of void callback RAX. Default file handling completes CREATE/CLEANUP/CLOSE with Information=0; zero READ/WRITE and missing default-queue handlers follow explicit framework policy.

WdfIoQueueReadyNotify registers one EvtIoQueueState callback for a manual queue; it receives WDFQUEUE and WDFCONTEXT at PASSIVE_LEVEL when the queued count changes from empty to nonempty, including while earlier retrieved requests remain driver-owned. Registration on a nonempty queue may notify immediately, while a stopped queue defers until Start. Duplicate registration or deregistration before Stop returns STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST; NULL deregisters after Stop.

WdfIoQueueFindRequest searches a manual queue without taking ownership and adds a framework reference on success; WdfObjectDereferenceActual releases that reference. WdfIoQueueRetrieveFoundRequest transfers ownership only while the request remains queued; cancellation removal returns STATUS_NOT_FOUND. Optional WDF_REQUEST_PARAMETERS reuse WdfRequestGetParameters layout. Framework file-object filtering and full file callbacks remain unsupported.

EvtIoCanceledOnQueue receives WDFQUEUE and WDFREQUEST for a request previously delivered to the driver and then forwarded or requeued, or explicitly enqueued from caller context. A never-delivered queued request is framework-completed with STATUS_CANCELLED without that callback. Cancellation transfers an eligible request to driver ownership; it must be completed inside the callback or later and cannot be requeued. Purge and queue-state notification wait for the callback and driver-owned request to finish.

The 40-byte WDF_REQUEST_PARAMETERS and input/output accessors preserve logical lengths, buffered aliases and existing direct MDL mappings; direct IOCTL input remains buffered. Completion validates first, then runs cleanup and child destruction before IRP retirement; new buffer/parameter accessors stop once completion begins, while saved buffers remain valid through cleanup. External WDF references preserve context without retaining completed IRP/queue ownership.

KMDF control-device READ/WRITE/IOCTL cancellation uses optional cancel_after_100ns, a nonnegative JSON integer at most INT64_MAX relative to submission in virtual 100 ns units. Zero acts after routing and before the guest I/O callback, including after caller-context enqueue and queue routing, unless routing completed first; completion before cancellation leaves cancel_requested_at_100ns null, otherwise reports record the actual absolute virtual time. WDM READ/WRITE/IOCTL cancellation sets the live IRP cancel bit and invokes a registered cancel routine at DISPATCH_LEVEL with the cancel spin lock held; IoCancelIrp invokes it synchronously and reports whether it ran. General queues and PnP cancellation remain unsupported.

WdfRequestMarkCancelableEx returns STATUS_CANCELLED without callback delivery for already canceled requests; successful WdfRequestUnmarkCancelable prevents later callback delivery while preserving observable cancellation state. WdfRequestIsCanceled requires an unmarked live request. After successful marking, completion requires successful unmarking or delivered cancellation, not merely a queued callback; delivered callbacks and workers may cooperate. A separate internal reference lasts through cancellation-callback return, retaining context after IRP retirement; final destruction continuations may wait.

Legacy void WdfRequestMarkCancelable invokes a real synchronous guest cancellation callback before returning for an already canceled IRP. Its nested API continuation supports waits, cleanup and final destruction; cancellation after registration remains scheduled. This matches the public source at PASSIVE_LEVEL with SynchronizationNone, while Microsoft directs drivers without automatic synchronization to use Ex; compatibility execution does not recommend this usage.

WdfRequestGetInformation/SetInformation share the original 64-bit IRP.IoStatus.Information with guest writes; Set only assigns and completion validates transfer length. CompleteWithInformation writes the authoritative field before cleanup, and cleanup edits through the saved raw IRP determine final Information even though its WDF getter returns zero then. GetIoQueue returns the current delivering queue while driver-owned, including a manual destination after retrieval; default GetFileObject returns NULL without inventing a WDF file object, and WdmGetIrp returns the original packet. Guest IoCompleteRequest/IofCompleteRequest cannot bypass framework completion.

Valid retained request handles during/after completion return zero from GetInformation/GetIoQueue; WdmMdl retrieval clears a valid output slot to NULL then returns STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR. SetInformation/GetFileObject/WdmGetIrp and existing buffer/parameter access remain rejected. Framework references preserve context, not completed IRP, MDL or buffer storage.

Input/output WdmMdl retrieval lazily describes existing SystemBuffer for buffered WRITE input, READ output and IOCTL input/output. Each direction is validated as nonempty before reuse; one cache per request preserves the first successful direction's ByteCount. The safe mapping helper returns the original VA; additional mapping, unmapping and driver freeing are rejected. Direct READ output, WRITE input and IOCTL output preserve IRP.MdlAddress without mapping on retrieval; direct IOCTL input uses the SystemBuffer cache. Completion retires descriptors with packet/buffers. Built physical PFNs are read-only; WDF MDL retrieval for METHOD_NEITHER remains unsupported.

active CFG validates packed sorted GFIDS metadata and enforces exact declared entry addresses plus known export thunks at check/dispatch helpers while preserving Win64 arguments; inactive instrumentation keeps guest fallback code; Windows CFG bitmap address rounding, XFG, export suppression and long-jump tables remain unsupported

Genuine KMDF lifecycle/control integration tests require separately acquired WDK 1.33 headers and unmodified entry/import libraries plus explicit NEVERD_KMDF_FIXTURE, NEVERD_KMDF_CFG_FIXTURE, NEVERD_KMDF_CONTROL_FIXTURE and NEVERD_KMDF_CONTROL_CFG_FIXTURE paths; missing fixtures skip visibly, SDK files are not distributed, and execution evidence remains Linux-only.

instruction, guest-memory, observation and wall-clock budgets apply across one concrete scenario; buffered/direct/neither requests may complete synchronously or through executed work-item and DPC callbacks after marked STATUS_PENDING; arbitrary concurrent public scenario submissions and PnP request cancellation, APCs, KMDF embedded user pointers, general KMDF PnP devices and driver-held queue power transitions, UMDF, full PnP/power, other interrupt modes, general hardware and other DMA interfaces remain unsupported

defer_callback_drain is a strict WDM or supported KMDF READ/WRITE/IOCTL Boolean that requires its dispatch to leave an IRP pending. It permits the next request on another file or the same asynchronous file to be submitted before callback draining; the next ordinary request or scenario end drains and finalizes the batch. Synchronous-file overlap, arbitrary thread preemption and external request arrival remain unsupported.

CREATE-only asynchronous_file sets an asynchronous FILE_OBJECT, clearing FO_SYNCHRONOUS_IO and omitting IRP_SYNCHRONOUS_API on its file IRPs. Such a file admits overlapping READ/WRITE/IOCTL transfers during explicit deferred draining, but CLEANUP/CLOSE require prior transfers to finalize. The model does not advance an implicit current byte offset on asynchronous files; byte_offset remains per request with zero default. Non-CREATE use of the field is rejected even when false. Synthetic, genuine WDK, C API and CLI cases cover this bounded same-file overlap.

wdm-x64-scheduled-v54 uses deterministic cooperative scheduling on CPU0 at returned-call and blocking-wait boundaries; DelayedWorkQueue workers and system threads execute at PASSIVE_LEVEL and DPC callbacks execute at DISPATCH_LEVEL with four guest arguments; no available producer for an incomplete pending request or infinite wait is a stalled model_error; work-item objects and device references retain separate lifetimes

PsCreateSystemThread admits bounded system-process threads with NULL ProcessHandle/ClientId and NULL or kernel-handle-only object attributes. Separate kernel handles and opaque thread-object pointers survive ZwClose and ObReferenceObjectByHandle until ObDereferenceObject; KeWaitForSingleObject observes nonalertable termination. PsTerminateSystemThread ends its own guest execution without returning, publishes exit status and signals the thread object. A normal start-routine return fails. Process identity is system PID 4 unless the thread explicitly attaches to a live requestor. General APC delivery, thread priorities, non-system process handles and typed object references remain unsupported.

KeInitializeSpinLock and five executive acquire/release/try APIs model resident, aligned x64 locks on CPU0. Ownership belongs to one guest execution, matching release variants restore the saved IRQL, and try-acquire returns false for a held lock. Guest writes, premature freeing, return or suspension while held stop explicitly. Contended blocking acquisition cannot progress in this cooperative profile and stops rather than spinning indefinitely; in-stack queued locks and cross-CPU contention remain unsupported.

The x64 WDK KeRaiseIrql macros and KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel/SynchLevel inline helpers call KfRaiseIrql; KeLowerIrql restores its returned value. The model accepts nested nondecreasing raises through HIGH_LEVEL on one execution, requires exact LIFO restoration, rejects lowering under a held lock, and rejects callback return or suspension with unmatched raises. API boundaries synchronize CR8 and inlined KeGetCurrentIrql observes the new value. This is deterministic CPU0 state, without instruction-level interrupt preemption or a general multiprocessor HAL.

KeEnterCriticalRegion/KeLeaveCriticalRegion and KeEnterGuardedRegion/KeLeaveGuardedRegion maintain bounded per-thread nested disable depths. KeAreApcsDisabled observes normal APC suppression by critical/guarded regions or an owned KMUTEX; KeAreAllApcsDisabled observes guarded regions or IRQL >= APC_LEVEL. New system threads begin with normal APCs disabled in one critical region. Unmatched leaves and callbacks returning with unbalanced regions fail explicitly. APC queuing and delivery remain unsupported.

KeInitializeSemaphore, KeReleaseSemaphore and KeReadStateSemaphore model resident counting semaphores with a positive limit, nonnegative initial count, exact previous-count return and one unit consumed per successful wait. Release accepts Increment=0 and Wait=FALSE only; over-limit adjustment raises STATUS_SEMAPHORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED without changing the count. General wait handoff, priority boosts and multiple-object waits remain unsupported.

KeInitializeMutex, KeReleaseMutex and KeReadStateMutex model a resident x64 KMUTEX whose owner is the current guest execution. Successful single-object waits acquire recursively, release returns the previous signed signal state, and final release signals the object. Release by another execution raises STATUS_MUTANT_NOT_OWNED; a held mutex rejects return, reinitialization and storage retirement. Level must be zero and Wait=TRUE handoff is unsupported. System-thread APC delivery and priority changes remain unsupported.

IoDeleteDevice defers physical retirement while attachment neighbors, retained request routes, live file objects or queued/running work-item references remain; deletion cannot create a new device lifetime or make stale work-item handles usable

full CPU contexts include SIMD/FPU/control state and each callback owns a separate guest stack, preserving multiple blocked frames while guest memory stays shared; Win64 callback entry passes the first four arguments in registers and additional arguments on the stack; foreign, expired and faulted contexts cannot resume execution

guest timers support relative/absolute deadlines, periodic expiration, rearm/cancel and notification/synchronization signals; virtual time advances to timer, wait and cancellation boundaries only while no callback/frame is ready; initialized event/timer/semaphore/mutex single-object waits support only nonalertable KernelMode with reason Executive, zero polling, finite relative/absolute and infinite waits; KernelMode nonalertable delay is modeled, while alertable and user-mode waits stop explicitly

KeSetEvent supports Increment=0 and Wait=FALSE only; event signal consumption and waiter wakeups remain distinct from callback return; DPC targets are restricted to CPU0, nonzero/infinite waits require IRQL <= APC_LEVEL, and pending dispatcher-object or wait references prohibit premature storage release

KernelAPIIRQL.def owns routine ceilings with argument-dependent checks in the API or memory owner; DPC registry calls, paged-pool allocation/free/access and Unicode DbgPrint conversions fail before mutation; supported ANSI output and nonpaged operations remain usable at DISPATCH_LEVEL; bounded callback stacks reject escape into suspended workers and armed extension timers prevent premature device retirement

timer expiration satisfies registered waits before a DPC can reset or rearm the signal; queued DPCs precede FIFO framework cancellation callbacks, which precede ordinary workers and resuming ready PASSIVE_LEVEL frames; IRP completion rejects release of request storage containing pending dispatcher objects before marking completion or invalidating buffers

strict scenario JSON rejects unknown and duplicate fields, invalid types, more than 64 requests, input or output buffers over 65536 bytes and total requested buffer bytes including direct_input over 512 KiB; requested load addresses require valid supported PE relocations

dynamic export lookup shares stable thunk identity with static imports; explicit kernel_exports availability overrides distinguish absent exports from present unmodeled routines; unspecified dynamic availability stops instead of changing driver capability branches

direct requests expose request-owned MDL system mappings with independent write/execute permissions; standalone driver MDLs can describe live nonpaged pool allocations and retain their original alias; IRP associations/chains, unbuilt PFN data, user mappings, general guest SEH and Windows Unicode case/code-page tables remain unsupported

an explicit registry scenario defines a bounded accessible ASCII tree with per-handle capabilities and observable key/value mutations; omitted registry availability stops; ACLs, privileges, alternate views, registry symbolic links, persistence and non-ASCII name folding remain unsupported

DbgPrint and DbgPrintEx read at most 32 guest variable arguments under Win64 widths; formatting is bounded to 512 output bytes and 1024 format bytes; float, %n and unsupported text conversions stop explicitly

reports preserve DriverEntry NTSTATUS separately from per-request dispatch and completion status and aggregate scenario_success; success in the model does not establish that a driver works under Windows
zero-output IOCTLs preserve driver-defined IoStatus.Information without treating it as a transfer length; information_hex preserves all 64 bits alongside the compatible numeric information field
CPU write records are attempted guest writes outside the stack, may include a faulting write and exclude model API writes; object snapshots describe observed state at termination
the existing C API remains initialization-only; the added scenario C API and CLI --scenario route share strict preflight, preserve the session image and require unchanged input files
current execution evidence is limited to Linux hosts with Clang and lld-link fixture tools; no macOS or Windows host validation is claimed and the Python SDK provides only raw ABI bindings

DriverPower.def and DriverPowerOperation share strict scenario and per-PDO response packet facts: query/set, device/system, D0/D3 or working/sleeping3, none/sleep action, explicit opaque 32-bit system_context, and required final bus_completion status with optional delay. System query to working is unsupported. Power requests are file-free and forbid transfer/cancellation fields. JSON/native preflight share type, enum, target and count checks.

The power execution profile requires DO_POWER_PAGABLE without DO_POWER_INRUSH on the captured route and PASSIVE_LEVEL dispatch and PoRequestPowerIrp. PoCallDriver forwards the original owned power IRP; Vista+ PoStartNextPowerIrp validates lifetime without inventing a serialization token. General policy, WAIT_WAKE, shutdown/hibernate, other states/actions, nonpageable/inrush routes, general hardware and KMDF power policy remain unsupported.

Optional initial_reported_device_power explicitly seeds D0/D3 notification state separately for the provider PDO and each first-associated guest DEVICE_OBJECT. PoSetPowerState returns and updates only that object's previous value, independently of lifecycle transactions; missing seed fails without guessing. D0 notification permits DISPATCH_LEVEL, D3 requires IRQL <= APC_LEVEL.

Each PDO owns an independent requested_device_power FIFO, at most 64 templates across all PDOs. Only an actual PoRequestPowerIrp matching the PDO queue-head minor and target consumes a device-type template; absent/mismatched policy fails and unused templates create no observation. Callback context never determines a parent. Actual children have separate IRPs and report rows with origin PoRequestPowerIrp and zero-based response_index; scenario rows use origin scenario and null response_index.

Real PoRequestPowerIrp Query/Set uses six API arguments with a null output-IRP pointer. Its terminal five-argument void callback receives the original API device, minor, state, context and a distinct completed IO_STATUS_BLOCK snapshot. Inline child completion can precede the API STATUS_PENDING return; callbacks may wait and retain their snapshot until return. A system S0 parent may complete before its independent D0 child; parent result and packet storage are not reused.

Reports add nullable power, per-row origin/response_index, explicit packet facts, device/system before/after, original requested_device_object and actual nullable bus status/receipt/completion times. Final PnP snapshots add device_power/system_power; live devices add nullable reported_device_power. scenario_success matches only scenario-origin count while requiring all actual scenario and child rows to complete successfully; unused FIFO entries do not fail the scenario.

Original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_power.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_POWER_FIXTURE/NEVERD_WDM_POWER_CFG_FIXTURE. Native normal/active-CFG rebasing covers Query/Set, independent delayed children, inline and S0-before-D0 completion, callback waits, workers, null callbacks, query failures and independent PDO notification/FIFO state. C API/CLI execute six scenario requests and three real children; missing artifacts skip explicitly and execution evidence remains Linux-only.

The actual IoInitializeRemoveLockEx/IoAcquireRemoveLockEx/IoReleaseRemoveLockEx/IoReleaseRemoveLockAndWaitEx exports model the WDK macro ABI, including separate size arguments for retail 32-byte and DBG 120-byte opaque locks. Initialization and AndWait require PASSIVE_LEVEL; acquire/release permit DISPATCH_LEVEL. Every lock belongs to the exact guest DEVICE_OBJECT extension containing its complete aligned storage, including before attachment; neither PDO lifecycle nor Tag shape supplies ownership.

KernelRemoveLocks is the sole registration/acquisition/drain authority, separate from DeviceLifecycle. NULL and repeated Tags count independently per lock and are never dereferenced; completed IRP addresses remain valid opaque Tags. AndWait closes admission and releases exactly one matching acquisition. Later acquire returns STATUS_DELETE_PENDING without a release obligation; the final release latches readiness before the releasing callback returns.

A typed RemoveLock wait suspends the real CPU frame and resumes through existing continuations. The bounded context check requires a related retained REMOVE route containing the owner and actual provider receipt, including virtual time zero, but not lower completion or live Tag memory. Lower queueing before provider receipt is explicitly unsupported; this is not full OutsideRemoveDevice/Driver Verifier enforcement. No producer is a stalled model error, not a synthetic callback, timeout or success.

REMOVE still requires closed files and finalized earlier requests in this serial profile, but no longer rejects all outstanding callbacks before dispatch. Workers may release a lock and then wait for the resumed remover. The request route survives AndWait, detach/delete and lower pending completion, and remaining execution frames must return before final route retirement. Teardown is preflighted before erasing request identity or releasing any device owner.

Unknown, unaligned, out-of-extension or overlapping lock storage, mismatched sizes, unmatched releases, duplicate drain and reinitialization fail explicitly without mutating valid state. Delete/Detach reject held acquisitions or unconsumed drain waits before changing DeletePending/topology. Unused initialized locks can retire in clean AddDevice failure; actual extension retirement unregisters storage. Drain never consumes genuine work-item/device references. Debug metadata does not enable Verifier timeout/high-water behavior.

Original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_remove_lock.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_REMOVE_LOCK_FIXTURE, NEVERD_WDM_REMOVE_LOCK_CFG_FIXTURE, NEVERD_WDM_REMOVE_LOCK_DBG_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_REMOVE_LOCK_DBG_CFG_FIXTURE. Native tests cover retail/DBG ABI, normal/active-CFG rebasing, opaque retired Tags, NULL/repeated Tags, DPC release, waiting workers, delayed lower removal, no-producer stalls, independent PDOs and clean AddDevice failure. C API/CLI use the unchanged PnP schema for synchronous/delayed lower completion and verify actual release/wait/drain/delete/resume order. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; evidence is Linux-only.

The synthetic register_bank bus accepts explicit memory resources with stable per-PDO id, raw_start, translated_start, length and registers. Each register requires offset, width, read_only/read_write access and initial value. DriverResources.h/.def own native types, spellings and limits; JSON and native options share validateDriverResources. Bounds are 8 resources per PDO/32 total, 256 registers per resource/4096 total, and 1..1048576 bytes per resource. Physical intervals cannot overflow; translated intervals never overlap globally, raw intervals cannot overlap within one PDO, and register intervals must fit without overlap. Widths1/2/4 and offsets/translated addresses are naturally aligned; values fit their declared width. Empty register arrays explicitly leave no accessible offsets.

Register-bank START receives separate read-only packed raw and translated CM_RESOURCE_LISTs with corresponding ordered Memory descriptors, one full header, Internal/bus0/version1/revision1, DeviceExclusive and READ_WRITE range flags. ResourceFree retains null lists. Each START from NotStarted/Stopped creates a new fixed-assignment epoch, published only at actual successful provider START completion before upper callbacks. Bank values initialize once per PDO and persist across unmap, STOP and restart. Failed START or successful STOP/REMOVE requires driver unmap before terminal IRP completion, allowing upper completion callbacks to unmap first; no implicit mapping cleanup hides a leak. Surprise arrival disables hardware/new maps immediately while allowing unmap.

KernelResources is the sole physical-assignment, epoch, presence and power authority. KernelMMIO owns bank values and aliases; KernelInterrupts owns connections, locks and pulses. Actual successful provider device-SET completion updates hardware accessibility before final upper lifecycle completion: D3 forbids register transactions but permits mapping, D0 additionally requires a live assignment. Power transitions neither reset register values nor discard mappings. PoSetPowerState notification remains a separate fact.

MmMapIoSpace uses NonCached; MmMapIoSpaceEx uses PAGE_NOCACHE with PAGE_READONLY/PAGE_READWRITE. Both accept exact translated subranges within one assignment and preserve page offset. Aliases share register state with independent permissions; MmUnmapIoSpace requires the original base/length. Monotonic address reservations prevent stale mapping reuse. Mapping/window or configured memory-budget exhaustion returns NULL; backend failures remain explicit errors. No arbitrary physical RAM, execute/cache variants, PCI configuration, ports, other interrupt modes, resource rebalance or other DMA interfaces is implied.

GuestMemory and UnicornBackend preflight whole original accesses and share a first-fault/stop latch with MMIO callbacks, preventing Unicorn width splitting or post-stop callbacks from producing effects. Exact scalar1/2/4 and real REP element transactions execute; holes, wrong widths, unaligned/partial/cross-mapping accesses, RO writes and instruction fetches fail before register effects. Modeled API memory accesses must also fit one aligned 1/2/4-byte transaction; larger bulk spans fail instead of being split into register accesses. Initial facts are reported under configuration.pnp_devices[].resources with lossless physical-address strings; runtime bank values are observed through actual guest I/O instead of a duplicate public state model.

The original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_resources.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_RESOURCE_FIXTURE/NEVERD_WDM_RESOURCE_CFG_FIXTURE and true scalar/REP accessors. Native normal/active-CFG rebasing covers packed lists, lower completion timing, aliases, page-tail mappings, STOP/restart persistence, independent PDOs, surprise cleanup and invalid accesses. Public C API/CLI reject invalid register facts before image loading and execute the 14-request driver-register-bank-scenario.json through two START epochs, preserving returned IOCTL bytes and exact map/unmap counts. C V1 struct and Python ctypes are unchanged because scenario_json is shared. Missing genuine artifacts skip explicitly; evidence remains Linux-only.

DriverResources.h / DriverResources.def and DriverInterrupts.h / DriverInterrupts.def define fixed register_bank memory and interrupt assignments. DriverScenario owns JSON/native preflight; DriverResult records initial configuration without duplicating observed bank state. KernelResources alone owns packed raw/translated assignments, resource epochs, physical presence and power. KernelMMIO owns persistent register values and independent mapping aliases; KernelInterrupts owns opaque connections, locks and explicit pulses. KernelModelResources builds read-only START packets and integrates actual provider completion: successful lower START publishes its epoch before upper callbacks, and actual provider device-SET updates D0/D3 accessibility. Failed START or STOP/REMOVE teardown is checked before terminal IRP completion, after upper callbacks can unmap and disconnect, without implicit cleanup. Surprise removal immediately denies hardware access. GuestMemory and UnicornBackend validate whole CPU/API transactions before MMIO effects and preserve the first fault latch. Fixed-assignment restart preserves bank values. Arbitrary RAM, resource rebalance, ports, shared/level/message interrupts and other DMA interfaces remain unsupported.

KernelInterrupts binds each explicit pulse to the connection token and resource epoch present at successful source request submission. KernelModelInterruptEvents preflights all same-time producer capacities before clock advancement or observation mutation, including exact framework cancellation callback counts; timers, provider completion and cancellation cannot silently consume the space reserved for an ISR. Actual provider hardware publication precedes pulse eligibility, and admitted interrupts precede DPCs and passive callbacks. The schedule remains cooperative: virtual time advances only while idle, and zero delay does not mean instruction preemption. KernelModelInterrupts decodes the legacy eleven-argument ABI and selected Ex fields, while KernelGuestCall gives interrupt callbacks a separate owner/token. ISR and synchronization callbacks hold the same nonrecursive lock at assigned DIRQL; nested CPU frames preserve caller IRQL/CR8, and BOOLEAN uses only AL. Manual locks require the same execution identity and saved IRQL, and a callback cannot return with a leaked lock. Armed pulses outlive their source IRP; disconnected, unavailable-epoch or D3 delivery records an explicit undelivered reason and stops, with no rebind or invented enable/ack register behavior. DriverResult.Interrupts contains independent observations, never synthetic IRPs or NTSTATUS completions.

The same register_bank provider can declare interrupts alone or alongside resources; at least one list must be nonempty. resource_free rejects an explicit interrupts field, including []. Each interrupt requires id, raw_vector, raw_level, raw_affinity, translated_vector, translated_level, translated_affinity, mode: "latched" and share: "device_exclusive". DriverInterrupts.h / DriverInterrupts.def own the types, spellings and limits: 8 interrupts per PDO / 32 total, per-PDO unique bounded ASCII IDs, globally exclusive translated vectors, raw level 0–65535 and translated DIRQL 3–12. Vectors retain all 32 bits without a guessed vector/IRQL relation. Both affinity masks must be 1: CPU0 and group0 are explicit provider facts. Raw and translated values are independent. Memory descriptors keep their order, followed by ordered interrupt descriptors in the same CM_RESOURCE_LIST; interrupt descriptors use type 2, DeviceExclusive sharing and LATCHED flags. This synthetic edge-triggered profile does not represent PCI shared level lines.

READ/WRITE/IOCTL requests may declare interrupt_events, each with explicit after_100ns, device_id and interrupt_id; other request kinds reject the field even when empty. At most 64 events per request / 1024 total are accepted, with nonnegative delay through INT64_MAX. Successful request submission anchors the delay and captures an already connected interrupt plus its PDO resource epoch. Events are independent external line pulses: source IRP completion does not cancel them, and register writes do not infer enable, status or acknowledgement. Time advances only while idle; due events run at the next supported callback boundary, so after_100ns: 0 promises no instruction-level preemption or delivery before the first guest instruction. Same-time producers are capacity-preflighted together; provider hardware publication precedes eligibility and ISR callbacks precede DPCs/workers. A lost connection, stale/unavailable epoch or physical D3 records undelivered_reason and stops as model_error; the event is never rebound or silently delayed.

IoConnectInterrupt uses its actual eleven arguments and the exact translated assignment. IoConnectInterruptEx supports FullySpecified (1), LineBased (2, one assigned line on the explicit PDO) and FullySpecifiedGroup (4, group 0); IoDisconnectInterruptEx requires the matching version/context. Registration and disconnection require PASSIVE_LEVEL. Only a private interrupt lock, exclusive latched mode, CPU0/group0 and no floating-state save are supported. Synchronization IRQL must equal the assigned DIRQL; LineBased zero selects that level. KINTERRUPT is opaque and its address is never reused. The real ISR receives (Interrupt, ServiceContext) and returns BOOLEAN from AL; FALSE is unclaimed, not NTSTATUS failure. KeSynchronizeExecution runs the real one-argument callback under the same lock at DIRQL and returns its BOOLEAN while restoring caller IRQL/CR8. KeAcquireInterruptSpinLock / KeReleaseInterruptSpinLock enforce nonrecursive ownership, the original execution and saved IRQL; leaked locks cannot cross callback return. Interrupt waits, caller-provided shared locks, shared/level/MSI/passive interrupts and instruction-level interrupt preemption remain unsupported. Failed START and successful STOP/REMOVE require disconnection before terminal completion; upper completion callbacks may tear down first, and disconnect never silently discards a queued DPC.

Reports separate declarations from observations. configuration.pnp_devices[].interrupts retains resources, and configuration.interrupt_events flattens input events with zero-based source_request_index (the configured request index) and event_index. Root interrupts rows add device_id, interrupt_id, epoch, absolute due_at_100ns, nullable occurred_at_100ns, delivered_at_100ns, returned_at_100ns, interrupt_object, return_value, claimed and undelivered_reason. claimed derives only from the actual low-byte return; timestamps are observations, not fabricated callback results. Every configured event must return without an undelivered failure for scenario_success; an unclaimed ISR remains valid. DPC effects appear through actual request completion, API calls and messages. The runnable interrupt scenario uses original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_interrupts.c with optional NEVERD_WDM_INTERRUPT_FIXTURE / NEVERD_WDM_INTERRUPT_CFG_FIXTURE: seven requests include delayed START, a pending IOCTL completed by ISR→DPC, file cleanup/close and removal. The existing C/Python scenario_json boundary and neverd_driver_options_v1 layout are unchanged. Missing genuine artifacts skip explicitly; execution evidence is Linux-only.

DriverDMA.h / DriverDMA.def add an optional dma object to a register_bank PDO, alongside its memory/interrupt assignments; DMA alone does not replace either resource list. All seven fields are explicit: address_bits (32 or 64), maximum_length (1–1048576 bytes), map_registers (1–256), alignment (power of two from 1–4096), logical_base (nonzero and page aligned), logical_length (page aligned, 4096–1073741824 bytes), and Boolean scatter_gather. The overflow-free aperture must fit the address width. Each PDO has an independent logical domain, so equal addresses on different devices do not alias. Translated MMIO resources must avoid the reserved model RAM range [0x1000000000, 0x1000100000). These declarations describe a coherent synthetic bus master, never host physical memory or a PCI device.

IoGetDmaAdapter accepts the historical DEVICE_DESCRIPTION version 0/1 fields for an Internal bus master and publishes a version-one DMA_ADAPTER with its actual 104-byte DMA_OPERATIONS table. Version 2/3 probes return NULL without reading a modern description tail. Each indirect method is bound to that exact live adapter, independently of kernel imports. Implemented methods are AllocateCommonBuffer, FreeCommonBuffer, GetDmaAlignment, GetScatterGatherList, PutScatterGatherList, PutDmaAdapter, AllocateAdapterChannel, MapTransfer, FlushAdapterBuffers and FreeMapRegisters. FreeAdapterChannel and ReadDmaCounter remain named traps because this profile has no subordinate/system DMA controller. Common-buffer allocation/free and alignment queries require PASSIVE_LEVEL; Get/PutScatterGatherList require DISPATCH_LEVEL, and adapter release permits IRQL through DISPATCH_LEVEL. x64 ignores CacheEnabled. Unsupported version probes, incompatible declared capabilities and documented allocation shortages return NULL; malformed or unmodeled interface selections and backend failures remain explicit errors.

KernelPhysicalMemory assigns at most 256 model physical pages of 4096 bytes to existing RAM. CPU virtual addresses, physical page identities and device logical addresses are distinct. Built MDL PFN arrays expose these shared identities read-only; unbuilt descriptors have no usable PFNs. Small neighboring allocations may share a PFN but retain separate byte ranges and lifetimes. Common buffers, pool storage and request buffers use the same bytes already owned by GuestMemory, without a second DMA copy. A live SG mapping pins its exact data range and descriptor. Completion, pool/MDL free and teardown reject live dependencies before retirement. Unmapping a direct MDL only revokes its CPU system mapping; DMA remains able to reach its locked backing. DmaWritable records the write-lock contract separately from CPU mapping permissions: device writes require direct READ/OUT_DIRECT or writable nonpaged storage; WRITE/IN_DIRECT do not gain that permission merely because their CPU mapping is writable.

GetScatterGatherList validates CurrentVa/Length against the MDL's original range and creates logical page fragments over its existing backing. Available map registers allow the real four-argument void AdapterListControl to run inline before the API returns; otherwise admission retains the data/descriptor and reserves a callback in the PDO's FIFO until resources are released. This profile has no StartIo ownership, so the callback's second IRP argument is NULL. Callback return does not release a mapping. CPU access to a live SG data range requires Put first; a callback waiting for map registers has not yet granted the device ownership of those bytes. PutScatterGatherList may run inside the callback; after Put, the driver may complete the request and release the last adapter while its callback continuation and device hold survive until return. Common buffers require their original adapter, length, logical address and CPU address when freed. Logical addresses are never reused during the session, including restart. A resource wait without a real producer stalls explicitly; it does not fabricate a completion or deadline.

Only READ/WRITE/IOCTL requests accept dma_events. Each event requires after_100ns, device_id, logical_address, direction and length; write_memory additionally requires exact-length data_hex, while read_memory rejects that field. Directions are from the device's perspective. Limits are 64 events per request, 1024 total, 16 MiB of total transaction bytes and 1 MiB per transaction; delay is nonnegative through INT64_MAX. Submission captures the PDO's current assigned epoch and anchors virtual time, but does not require a mapping that the forthcoming dispatch has yet to create. Delivery resolves the complete live logical range and direction, requires physical D0, and validates all backing bytes before any transaction effect. Source IRP completion does not cancel an event. Missing/released mappings, stale epochs, surprise removal or D3 record a failure and stop; events neither rebind nor invent an interrupt, register protocol or IRP completion. At one scheduled boundary, provider hardware publication precedes DMA bytes, which precede independently declared interrupt pulses. Timing remains cooperative, not instruction-level preemption.

Reports retain configuration.pnp_devices[].dma and flattened configuration.dma_events. Root dma_transfers rows identify source_request_index, event_index, device_id, epoch, logical_address, direction, length and due_at_100ns, with nullable occurred_at_100ns, completed_at_100ns, mapping, adapter and failure_reason; data_hex contains actual transferred bytes. Every declared transaction must finish without failure for scenario_success. The DMA scenario uses original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_dma.c with optional NEVERD_WDM_DMA_FIXTURE / NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CFG_FIXTURE, exercising a common buffer through actual adapter pointers and a separately declared ISR→DPC completion. C/Python still use scenario_json without changing neverd_driver_options_v1. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; evidence is Linux-only. Subordinate controllers, V2/V3 methods, hardware descriptor engines, general KMDF DMA and other device models remain unsupported.

DriverDMA.h / DriverDMA.def own explicit per-PDO capabilities and independent external transactions. KernelPhysicalMemory registers exact live RAM allocations, assigns shared page identities and pins byte ranges; MDLs are views of that authority, not copied buffers. GuestMemory / UnicornBackend provide whole-span backing access that bypasses CPU permissions without changing them, rejects MMIO/running/reentrant or faulted access, and latches unexpected backend failures. KernelDMA owns independent logical domains, adapter-bound method identities, common/SG mappings, map-register admission and callback references; KernelDMAEvents resolves captured PDO epochs at actual delivery. KernelModelPhysicalMemory, KernelModelDMA and KernelModelDMATransfers bridge original allocation/MDL ownership and real indirect guest callbacks. Available SG resources permit inline delivery, while queued callbacks reserve identity and capacity until FIFO promotion. Mapping and callback lifetimes are separate: Put can release data/descriptor pins before callback return, and callback retention does not keep completed IRPs alive. DmaWritable records lock intent independently of CPU mapping permissions. Same-time provider publication precedes DMA RAM effects and then interrupt eligibility. Resource epochs/presence/power remain solely in KernelResources; DMA does not infer vendor registers, assert an IRQ, complete an IRP or own a second lifecycle. Logical addresses are never recycled, and transaction validation failures retain observations without changing RAM. The first interface is coherent common-buffer and version-one SG DMA over bounded model RAM; general hardware, subordinate controllers and other DMA interfaces remain unsupported.

AllocateAdapterChannel requires DISPATCH_LEVEL and reserves an opaque non-NULL map-register token. Common buffers, SG lists and channel reservations share the same per-PDO quota and FIFO. Success accepts a real immediate or queued AdapterControl; an excessive requested count returns STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES without a callback. One unfinished allocation callback is allowed per guest device, and calling AllocateAdapterChannel from AdapterControl is rejected, including through a nested callback. The callback's four arguments contain the actual DEVICE_OBJECT.CurrentIrp snapshot taken at registration. That exact eight-byte field is writable on guest devices; zero or a live IRP routed to the device is accepted. A queued callback retains that packet until entry, after which the callback may complete it. The profile still has no StartIo; the separate SG callback's unused IRP argument remains NULL.

AdapterControl returns a 32-bit IO_ALLOCATION_ACTION; high RAX bits are ignored, and the action never replaces AllocateAdapterChannel's STATUS_SUCCESS. DeallocateObject releases unused or fully flushed registers on callback return. DeallocateObjectKeepRegisters retains them until FreeMapRegisters uses the exact adapter, token and original count. Returning KeepObject requires an unmodeled system controller and fails explicitly. The newly delivered allocation cannot be freed as retained before its callback returns; a different previously retained allocation may be freed when its own contract permits. Callback identity, retained registers and active mapped bytes have separate lifetimes, all checked before adapter or device teardown.

MapTransfer and FlushAdapterBuffers permit IRQL through DISPATCH_LEVEL; channel allocation and register free require DISPATCH_LEVEL. MapTransfer takes an MDL-relative index, reads and updates an actual ULONG length and returns the logical address by value. The bounded SG profile returns one backing-page fragment per call; contiguous subsequent indices in the same MDL and direction extend one operation. Non-SG maps the entire requested extent in one call if it fits the reserved count, without shortening it. The first map reserves a nonreused logical aperture sized to the register reservation; other allocations can interleave without overlapping it. All fragments share one growing physical pin. Device transactions can span the full currently mapped operation, while CPU access, MDL free and completion that retires pinned storage remain blocked until aggregate flush. Flush must match the initial index, MDL, direction and total actual mapped length. It releases mapped bytes without releasing registers, so the retained token can support another operation. Partial flushes, mixed-MDL operations and other MapTransfer patterns are outside this profile, rather than assumed invalid on every Windows system.

KeFlushIoBuffers validates a live locked/nonpaged MDL. The modeled platform is coherent, so either ReadOperation or DmaOperation value needs no separate cache copy; this call does not release DMA ownership or replace FlushAdapterBuffers. The channel scenario runs original driver_wdm_dma_channel.c through two MapTransfer calls, one cross-page device transaction, a separately declared IRQ/DPC, aggregate flush and exact register release. Genuine normal/CFG images use NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_CFG_FIXTURE.

The original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_dma_channel.c and optional NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_FIXTURE/NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_CFG_FIXTURE exercise real translated bus-master channel calls, aggregate fragments, retained-register reuse and shared common/SG/channel admission. Native normal/CFG/rebased runs and the seven-request C API/CLI example validate the bounded profile; Python uses the same scenario_json interface. Missing fixtures skip explicitly and evidence remains Linux-only.

ExRaiseStatus, ExRaiseAccessViolation and ExRaiseDatatypeMisalignment produce typed guest exceptions without a normal API return. ExRaiseStatus uses only the low NTSTATUS dword; the wrappers use STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION and STATUS_DATATYPE_MISALIGNMENT. The selected profile follows the individual Microsoft DDI ceilings APC_LEVEL for ExRaiseStatus and PASSIVE_LEVEL for the wrappers, while acknowledging that some WDK SAL annotations permit APC_LEVEL for the wrappers. API traces retain a null result and record the raised code in detail.

KernelSEH plans bounded x64 version-one C catch-all transfers over the loader's existing preferred-base metadata. It selects constant EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER scopes in table order, translates checked rebased addresses and restores supported nonvolatile GPR saves across ordinary helpers. DriverSession commits only a fully validated plan at a healthy API boundary, within the current execution stack. Actual guest handler bodies and enclosing-handler reraises execute; GetExceptionCode observes the raised code. Encountered filters/finally, GS/C++ personalities, chained or incomplete records, prologue unwinding and XMM restoration stop explicitly. Uncaught API or supported user-memory exceptions are model_error; other backend memory, interrupt and invalid-instruction faults remain terminal. WDM METHOD_NEITHER has separate user input/output allocations, ProbeForRead/Write, in-context catchable CPU faults, independent user MDL locks and shared kernel aliases. KMDF METHOD_NEITHER exposes caller-context unsafe user buffers and request-owned locked WDFMEMORY aliases; embedded user pointers and arbitrary processes remain unsupported.

The original genuine-WDK /GS- driver_wdm_seh.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_SEH_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_SEH_CFG_FIXTURE. Native normal/active-CFG/rebased cases exercise all three exports, helper nonvolatile restoration, nested and reraised handlers, unhandled exceptions and explicit filter/finally/CPU-fault rejection. C API/CLI runs docs/examples/driver-seh-scenario.json with null raised-call results and actual handler messages. pluginsdk/python/tests/test_driver_seh_integration.py uses the existing JSON binding and optional NEVERD_TEST_LIBNEVERD / NEVERD_TEST_WDM_SEH_FIXTURE / NEVERD_TEST_WDM_SEH_CFG_FIXTURE inputs. Missing fixtures skip explicitly; evidence is Linux-only and does not establish general SEH.

The original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_neither.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_NEITHER_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_NEITHER_CFG_FIXTURE. Native normal/active-CFG and preferred/rebased runs verify six packet/probe/CPU-fault/locked-MDL paths. Backend and request-owner tests verify shared alias bytes, independent pins, write protection, completion output and terminal kernel faults. C API/CLI and Python execute docs/examples/driver-neither-scenario.json and verify plain and locked-alias output bytes. Missing external images skip explicitly; Linux evidence does not establish arbitrary Windows process memory.

A nonempty WDM METHOD_NEITHER IOCTL may independently set user_input_access and user_output_access to read_write (default), read_only or no_access. These explicit page facts are applied after buffer initialization and before guest dispatch. No-access still retains a non-NULL caller pointer and RAM backing, so ProbeForRead can pass its numerical check before a CPU read faults, while ProbeForWrite and MmProbeAndLockPages raise access violations according to page rights. Strict JSON/native validation rejects rights on buffered/direct IOCTLs, wrong directions, empty buffers, unknown values and wrong types. The original WDK fixture runs CPU/probe/MDL negative paths through normal/CFG and preferred/rebased images; C/CLI/Python observe completed failing statuses without terminal backend faults. Caller-context restrictions keep raw user pointers unavailable in ordinary workers; a work item with a live requesting IRP can explicitly attach to that process for bounded raw user-memory access, while locked MDL system aliases remain independently usable. Optional user_unmap_after_dispatch revokes original user virtual access after dispatch returns and before queued work/cancellation; locked MDL aliases retain physical bytes and an unmapped output has no caller-visible output_hex. Synthetic requestor_process_id distinguishes bounded caller contexts; IoGetRequestorProcessId retains the file IRP identity and PsGetCurrentProcessId distinguishes foreground from modeled system work-item execution. requestor_exit_after_dispatch revokes every original VA of that identity before callbacks, while pinned MDL aliases can still complete or cancel. Later new I/O from an exited identity is rejected; explicit CLEANUP/CLOSE remain available, with no inferred handle rundown or cancellation. Arbitrary process address spaces, attachment outside system work items, unmap timing and VA reuse remain unsupported.

READ/WRITE on a WDM device with neither DO_BUFFERED_IO nor DO_DIRECT_IO uses the original caller address only through IRP.UserBuffer. WRITE carries initialized user input and READ a separate user output; neither creates a SystemBuffer or implicit MDL. User page rights apply to WRITE input or READ output only, and explicit rights on a buffered/direct device stop before guest dispatch. A genuine WDK normal/CFG fixture probes and accesses both directions under x64 SEH, including read-only/no-access failures, at preferred and rebased image addresses. C API, CLI and Python observe the same report bytes and request statuses. Deferred raw access still requires locking; general process address spaces remain unsupported.

The genuine WDK neither fixture marks an IOCTL pending after user MDLs are locked in caller context. Its PASSIVE_LEVEL work item reads/writes only through the shared kernel aliases, unlocks and frees the MDLs and work item, then completes the original IRP. The separate raw-user-pointer worker path stops explicitly because queued work does not inherit the requesting process context; an explicit IoGetRequestorProcess / KeStackAttachProcess / KeUnstackDetachProcess pair can access a live requestor with matching APC storage. Native normal/CFG preferred/rebased, C API/CLI and Python paths distinguish these outcomes; exited requestors, unmatched APC states and complex operations while attached fail explicitly. Scheduled WDM cancellation and driver-initiated IoCancelIrp use one IRP.Cancel/CancelRoutine state; a registered callback runs with the cancel spin lock held at DISPATCH_LEVEL, must release with CancelIrql before completion or return, and is ordered before pending workers. Genuine WDK normal/CFG/rebased, C API/CLI and Python cases cover canceled locked MDLs, completion-first, synchronous return values and an invalid IRQL release.
